pointBasis: UN WUP 2025 population-weighted settlement centroid; this is not a municipal boundary or a parcel-coverage claim.
name: Okara
registryBasis: Punjab Land Records Authority/Board of Revenue and the official Punjab PULSE map provide Okara district cadastral-map services with village selectors. PULSE Feature Layer 25 returned a complete polygon at the exact WUP point (OBJECTID 10854687), establishing public geometry presence. Khasra_ID and Mouza_ID are zero, so a legal/native parcel identity is not verified; the portal’s indicative/non-legal notice is retained as a boundary-status caveat.
scopeLimits: 15 valid distinct public cadastral-reference polygons verified in thirteen bounded 0.001-degree cells around the unchanged WUP settlement locator. Complete bounded manifest paging, forced three-row pages, all 15 fresh source-ID reads, explicit absence, footprint and source binding passed in 58 requests. Independent metric EPSG:32643 GEOS found all geometries valid and distinct, with no sampled overlaps above 0.01 m² or operation errors. Public source-native OBJECTID is the cadastral-reference geometry identity, not a legal Khasra/Mouza key. Returned legal key fields are zero and are not promoted to legal identifiers. The real runtime adapter uses the documented anonymous public-viewer reader bootstrap; reader tokens stay in memory, simultaneous reads share one bootstrap, and renewal occurs within thirty seconds because publisher expiry omits a timezone. All request evidence omits token values. Six headless reader tests verify renewal, coalescing, endpoint confinement, unchanged geometry, blocked responses and safe errors. Native source CRS is EPSG:3857 (ArcGIS WKID102100). The original exact-point sample is topologically identical to fresh complete geometry: ring coordinate order differs, while projected symmetric difference and Hausdorff distance are both zero. Citywide completeness, legal title, survey accuracy, currentness and long-term GIS key continuity remain unverified.
remainingUncertainty: Citywide completeness, legal title, currentness, survey accuracy and long-term native GIS identity continuity remain unverified.

executedQueries.executionMethod: Language-specific web search and first-party source inspection; public service routes were tested only with city-level or exact WUP locator inputs.

executedQueries.query: Okara Punjab official cadastral parcel map PULSE Punjab Land Records public GIS
executedQueries.scope: Cross-check local registry/map evidence and distinguish an identified public parcel feature from general/topographic or application-only records.
executedQueries.result: Official Punjab Land Records provides village-wise cadastral maps with District/Tehsil/Village selectors. The official Punjab PULSE Okara polygon layer returned one complete full polygon at the exact WUP point (OBJECTID 10854687; Khasra_ID=0; Mouza_ID=0). The service OBJECTID is preserved as a transport identifier, while legal parcel identity and runtime qualification remain unverified; PULSE labels lines indicative/non-legal.
executedQueries.executionMethod: English-language web search and first-party source/service inspection; no personal, owner, address, or property-specific query inputs submitted.

officialSources.observation: Official Punjab Land Records cadastral map page offers district/tehsil/village selectors.
Official Punjab PULSE map lists cadastral-map layers and cautions that mapped lines are indicative, not legal boundaries.
Okara polygon layer metadata returned HTTP 200; fields were reviewed and unsafe owner/account-type fields excluded from queries.

Exact WUP query returned HTTP 200 polygon response; safe IDs Khasra_ID and Mouza_ID were both zero, so it does not verify a valid parcel. A 200m nearby query restricted to Khasra_ID > 0 returned no features.

geometryEvidence: Punjab PULSE Cadastral Maps service, ArcGIS Feature Layer 25 named Okara, returned one full esriGeometryPolygon at the exact WUP point. Schema: OBJECTID esriFieldTypeOID; objectIdField/globalIdField metadata are null; Khasra_ID and Mouza_ID are integer legal/cadastral fields but both returned zero. OBJECTID 10854687 is preserved as the service transport identifier, not asserted as legal/native parcel identity. The point response has one 41-vertex ring. No owner/address/account-like Khewat_ID field was requested or retained.
